records.literal_gloss: And again he began to teach beside the sea.

en.L: And again {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} began to teach beside the sea.
en.B: Once more {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} began teaching by the lake.
en.R: Another time Jesus began to teach beside Lake Galilee.

vi.L: Và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} lại bắt đầu giảng dạy bên [bờ] biển.
vi.B: Một lần nữa, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} bắt đầu giảng dạy bên bờ hồ.
vi.R: Một lần khác, Đức Giê-xu bắt đầu dạy dỗ bên bờ hồ Ga-li-lê.

ko.L: 그리고 그분이 다시 바닷가에서 가르치기 시작하셨다.
ko.B: 예수께서 다시 바닷가에서 가르치기 시작하셨다.

es.L: Y otra vez comenzó a enseñar junto al mar.
es.B: Una vez más comenzó a enseñar a la orilla del lago.
es.R: En otra ocasión, Jesús comenzó a enseñar a la orilla del lago de Galilea.

fr.L: Et de nouveau {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} se mit à enseigner au bord de la mer.
fr.B: Une fois encore, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} se mit à enseigner au bord de la mer.
fr.R: Une autre fois, Jésus a commencé à enseigner au bord du lac de Galilée.

sw.L: Na tena alianza kufundisha kando ya bahari.
sw.B: Kwa mara nyingine alianza kufundisha kando ya ziwa.
sw.R: Siku nyingine Yesu alianza kufundisha kando ya Ziwa Galilaya.

decisions.choice: the sea: the Sea of Galilee, a freshwater lake
decisions.reason: Mark calls the lake of Galilee "the sea", as in 1:16 and 3:7.

decisions.choice: again: Jesus teaches by the lake once more
decisions.reason: He had taught crowds by the lake before (2:13; 3:7-9).

decisions.choice: the lake (B); Lake Galilee (R)
decisions.reason: As in chapters 1-3, Balanced and Readable call it a lake, which is what it is.

decisions.choice: "biển" (L); "hồ" (B); "hồ Ga-li-lê" (R) for the sea (whole chapter)
decisions.reason: As in 3:7: Literal keeps Mark's word; Balanced and Readable say what it is, a freshwater lake. At 4:39 and 4:41 Balanced keeps "biển", where Jesus commands the sea itself, as the English Balanced does.

decisions.choice: "{{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}" for Jesus in the narrative; Jesus says "Ta", calls the disciples "các con", and they call him "Thầy" and themselves "chúng con" (whole chapter)
decisions.reason: The forms of address the Vietnamese style guide (section 6) sets for the Gospels, as in the Vietnamese John. The narrator's "đã" is left out at Literal where Mark tells a past event in the present (4:1, 4:13, 4:35-38), as the guide sets for the historic present.

decisions.choice: No deity_pronoun spans in Korean; the narrative honours Jesus with "께서" and -시-, Jesus speaks in the plain style (해라체), the disciples speak to him in 합쇼체, and Mark's historic presents stay present only at Literal ("모여든다", "말씀하신다", "간다"), through chapter 4
alternatives: capitalised pronoun spans as in English
decisions.reason: Korean has no capital letters, so the deity_pronoun setting has nothing to change (style guide, sections 4 and 7). Literal keeps Mark's present tense in narrative (4:1, 4:13, 4:35-38); Balanced and Readable use the past. Recorded once for the chapter.

decisions.choice: "바다" (L, B); "갈릴리 호수" (R) for the Sea of Galilee, through chapter 4
decisions.reason: "바다" is the established Korean name ("갈릴리 바다") and keeps Mark's word; Readable calls it a lake, which is what it is, as the Korean John does at 6:1 and 21:1.

decisions.choice: deity_pronoun spans on every separate pronoun for Jesus; none on verb endings or on pronouns joined to a verb
decisions.reason: The rule for Mark set at 1:2: where Spanish leaves the subject in the verb ("comenzó"), the English span on "he" has no counterpart; every pronoun Spanish writes for Jesus (él, lo, le, su, mí, mi, te, tu) carries the span, except one joined to the end of a verb. A sentence-initial pronoun is written plain.

decisions.choice: el mar (L); el lago (B); el lago de Galilea (R)
decisions.reason: Mark calls the lake a sea (meaning decision m1). Literal keeps his word; Balanced and Readable say what it was, as the English does. The same throughout the chapter.

decisions.choice: narration in the passé simple (L, B), with Literal keeping Mark’s present tense ("se rassemble", "il dit", "ils l’emmènent", "ils le réveillent"); passé composé (R); speech in the passé composé at every level (for the whole chapter)
decisions.reason: As in the French of John and of Mark 3: the passé simple is the normal tense of written narrative; Literal keeps the present where Mark tells a past event in the present (4:1, 4:13, 4:35-38). Readable uses the passé composé, the narrative tense of spoken French.

decisions.choice: the deity_pronoun span on every French pronoun for Jesus, subject "il" included, and on "le", "l’", "lui", "te", "t’", "moi", "mes" (for the whole chapter)
decisions.reason: French must write the subject pronoun, so "il" for Jesus carries the span wherever the English "he" does, and also where French needs a pronoun the English lacks. A pronoun at the start of a sentence is written plainly with its capital.

decisions.choice: la mer (L, B); le lac de Galilée, le lac (R) (for the whole chapter)
decisions.reason: As in the French of John (6:16) and Mark 3:7: Literal and Balanced keep "la mer", the Greek word and the usual French name of this lake (meaning decision m1); Readable says "le lac" so young readers do not picture the ocean.

decisions.choice: bahari (L); ziwa (B); Ziwa Galilaya (R)
decisions.reason: As in 3:7: Mark calls the lake of Galilee "the sea" (m1). Literal keeps "bahari"; Balanced says "ziwa" (lake) and Readable names it. The same in 4:39 and 4:41.

decisions.choice: deity_pronoun spans only on free pronouns and possessives (yake, wake, kwake, naye)
alternatives: a span on every pronoun, as in English
decisions.reason: Swahili marks most pronouns for Jesus inside the verb ("alianza", "wakamwamsha"), and a prefix cannot take a capital, so this chapter has fewer setting spans than the English.

source.text: καὶ συνάγεται πρὸς αὐτὸν ὄχλος πλεῖστος, ὥστε αὐτὸν εἰς πλοῖον ἐμβάντα καθῆσθαι ἐν τῇ θαλάσσῃ, καὶ πᾶς ὁ ὄχλος πρὸς τὴν θάλασσαν ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς ἦσαν.

records.literal_gloss: And is gathered together to him a crowd very great, so that he into a boat having embarked sat in the sea, and all the crowd toward the sea on the land were.

en.L: And a very great crowd gathers to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, so that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} got into a boat and sat [in it] on the sea, and the whole crowd was beside the sea on the land.
en.B: The crowd that gathered around {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} was so enormous that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} stepped into a boat and sat in it out on the water, while all the people stayed on the shore by the lake.
en.R: A very large crowd came together around {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. So Jesus stepped into a boat. He sat down in it, out on the water. All the people stood on the shore by the lake.

vi.L: Và một đoàn dân rất đông tụ họp đến với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, đến nỗi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} xuống một chiếc thuyền và ngồi [trong thuyền] trên biển, còn cả đoàn dân thì ở trên đất liền, bên bờ biển.
vi.B: Đoàn dân tụ họp quanh {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đông đến nỗi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} phải bước xuống một chiếc thuyền và ngồi trong thuyền ngoài mặt hồ, còn tất cả dân chúng thì ở trên bờ, sát mép nước.
vi.R: Một đám đông rất lớn tụ họp quanh {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. Vì vậy, Đức Giê-xu bước xuống một chiếc thuyền. Ngài ngồi trong thuyền, ở ngoài mặt hồ. Còn mọi người thì đứng trên bờ hồ.

ko.L: 그러자 아주 큰 무리가 그분께 모여든다. 그래서 그분은 배에 올라 바다에 [떠서] 앉으셨고, 온 무리는 바다를 향하여 뭍에 있었다.
ko.B: 아주 많은 무리가 예수께 모여들었다. 그래서 예수께서는 배에 오르셔서 물 위에 띄운 배에 앉으셨고, 무리는 모두 바닷가 뭍에 있었다.
ko.R: 아주 많은 사람들이 예수 둘레에 모여들었다. 그래서 예수께서는 배에 오르셨다. 그리고 물 위에 떠 있는 배 안에 앉으셨다. 사람들은 모두 호숫가에 서 있었다.

es.L: Y se reúne alrededor de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} una multitud muy grande, de modo que subió a una barca y se sentó [en ella] sobre el mar, y toda la multitud estaba junto al mar, en tierra.
es.B: La multitud que se reunió a {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} alrededor era tan enorme que subió a una barca y se sentó en ella, sobre el agua, mientras toda la gente se quedaba en tierra, a la orilla del lago.
es.R: Una multitud muy grande se reunió alrededor de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}. Por eso Jesús subió a una barca. Se sentó en ella, sobre el agua. Toda la gente se quedó en la orilla del lago.

fr.L: Et une foule très nombreuse se rassemble auprès de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, de sorte que, montant dans une barque, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} s’assit sur la mer, et toute la foule était près de la mer, sur la terre.
fr.B: La foule qui s’assembla autour de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} fut si grande qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} monta dans une barque et s’y assit, sur l’eau, tandis que toute la foule restait sur le rivage, au bord de la mer.
fr.R: Une très grande foule s’est rassemblée autour de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}. Alors Jésus est monté dans une barque. Il s’est assis dedans, sur l’eau. Tous les gens se tenaient sur la rive, au bord du lac.

sw.L: Na umati mkubwa mno unakusanyika {{deity_pronoun:kwake|Kwake}}, hata akaingia katika mashua akaketi ndani yake baharini; na umati wote ulikuwa kando ya bahari, juu ya nchi kavu.
sw.B: Umati uliokusanyika kumzunguka ulikuwa mkubwa mno, hata akapanda mashua, akaketi ndani yake majini, na watu wote wakabaki ufuoni kando ya ziwa.
sw.R: Umati mkubwa sana wa watu ulikusanyika kumzunguka. Kwa hiyo Yesu alipanda mashua. Akaketi ndani yake, majini. Watu wote walisimama ufuoni kando ya ziwa.

decisions.choice: gathers: a present tense telling a past event
alternatives: the crowd is still gathering now
decisions.reason: Mark often tells past events in the present tense to make the story vivid. The sense is past.

decisions.choice: very great: the largest crowd yet
alternatives: the greatest crowd of all time
decisions.reason: The form is a superlative used to mean "very large".

decisions.choice: sat: teachers sat to teach
decisions.reason: A Jewish teacher sat while his hearers listened (Matthew 5:1; Luke 4:20). The boat kept the crowd from pressing on him, as 3:9 planned.

decisions.choice: gathered (B); came together (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable tell the story in the past tense.

decisions.choice: 바다에 [떠서] 앉으셨고
decisions.reason: Korean cannot say that someone sat "on the sea" without a verb for being afloat; Literal brackets it.

decisions.choice: present tense kept (L); past tense (B, R): se reúne / se reunió
decisions.reason: Mark often tells past events in the present tense (meaning decision m1). Literal keeps it; Balanced and Readable use the past, as Spanish stories do. This applies throughout the chapter.

decisions.choice: historic present kept at Literal (unakusanyika, anawaambia); past at Balanced and Readable
decisions.reason: Mark tells past events in the present (m1). Literal keeps the present so readers can see it; Balanced and Readable use the narrative past. This holds for the whole chapter (4:13, 4:35-38).

ko.L: 그리고 그분은 비유로 그들에게 많은 것을 가르치고 계셨고, 그분의 가르침 가운데서 그들에게 말씀하셨다.

es.B: Usaba parábolas para enseñarles muchas cosas, y mientras enseñaba les decía:
es.R: Les enseñó muchas cosas contándoles historias. Mientras enseñaba, les dijo:

fr.B: Il leur enseignait beaucoup de choses au moyen de paraboles, et, dans {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} enseignement, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur disait :

sw.B: Aliwafundisha mambo mengi kwa kutumia mifano, na alipokuwa akifundisha aliwaambia,
sw.R: Aliwafundisha mambo mengi kwa mifano, yaani hadithi fupi zenye mafundisho. Alipokuwa akifundisha, aliwaambia,

decisions.choice: parables: stories or sayings that compare one thing with another
decisions.reason: A parable sets a picture from daily life beside a truth about God's kingdom. The word can also mean a riddle or dark saying, which matters in 4:11.

decisions.choice: was teaching, was saying: the teaching went on for some time
decisions.reason: The verbs describe ongoing action. Mark gives a sample of what Jesus said.

decisions.choice: stories
decisions.reason: Readable calls the parables stories, as it does from 3:23.

decisions.choice: "ngụ ngôn" (L, B); "kể chuyện", "câu chuyện" (R) for parables (whole chapter)
decisions.reason: As in 3:23: "ngụ ngôn" is the usual modern word for Jesus' parables; "ví dụ" now means "example". In this chapter the parables are stories, so Readable says "câu chuyện", as the English Readable says "stories".

decisions.choice: "비유" at every level, Readable included
decisions.reason: "비유" is the established Korean word and is plain enough for new readers once explained (Mark 3:23 Readable); keeping it at Readable lets 4:10-13 and 4:33-34 speak of the same thing as here.

decisions.choice: parábolas (L, B); historias (R)
decisions.reason: As in English: Readable calls the parables of this chapter stories. The same throughout the chapter.

decisions.choice: paraboles (L, B); des histoires (R) (for the whole chapter)
decisions.reason: "Parabole" is the French word (meaning decision m1). Readable says "histoires", as the English Readable says "stories", since in this chapter most of the parables are short stories of sowing and growth.

decisions.choice: mifano at every level; Readable explains it once as "hadithi fupi zenye mafundisho"
decisions.reason: As in 3:23, "mfano" (a comparison, a parable) is kept at every level so the word that runs through this chapter stays the same. Readable explains it once as "short stories with a lesson", where the English Readable says "stories".

en.L: "Listen!
en.B: "Listen!
en.R: "Listen to me!

vi.B: "Hãy lắng nghe!
vi.R: "Hãy nghe đây!

ko.L: "들어라!
ko.B: "잘 들어라!
ko.R: "내 말을 잘 들어라!

es.L: «¡{{plural_you:Escuchen|Escuchad}}!
es.B: «¡{{plural_you:Escuchen|Escuchad}}!
es.R: «¡{{plural_you:Escúchenme|Escuchadme}}!

fr.L: « Écoutez !

fr.R: « Écoutez-{{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} !

sw.L: "Sikilizeni!
